blocks.text: 1. Query Rewriting
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447443246-558263596.png
Query rewriting, covering how a query can be reformulated rather than just extended, takes a more thorough approach to improving the query itself.
It replaces a query's original wording with a clearer, more retrieval friendly version.
2. Extending Versus Replacing
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447443246-207514167.png
Query expansion added terms on top of the original query.
Query rewriting instead replaces the query's own wording entirely with a better version.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Technique","What it changes"],"rows":[["Query expansion","Adds related terms alongside the original query"],["Query rewriting","Replaces the original query's wording entirely"]]}

blocks.text: 3. Why Raw User Queries Are Often Messy

blocks.alt: Why Raw User Queries Are Often Messy
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447443247-748345019.png
Real user queries often contain typos, incomplete sentences, or ambiguous pronouns.
That messiness can confuse both dense and sparse retrieval alike.
4. Rewriting With An LLM
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447443432-378024806.png
As with LLM based query expansion, a language model can rephrase a query into clearer, more complete language.
This turns a fragment or typo laden question into a well formed retrieval query.
5. Resolving Ambiguous Pronouns
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447443433-346031014.png
A query like "how do I cancel it" leaves "it" completely undefined on its own.
Rewriting with conversation context can resolve that pronoun into the actual subject.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A follow up question like "how do I cancel it" after discussing a subscription earlier in a conversation rewrites into "how do I cancel my subscription," a form retrieval can actually work with effectively.

blocks.text: 6. Normalizing Phrasing Across Queries
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447443434-113059895.png
As with text normalization, rewriting can standardize casing, terminology, and structure.
This makes retrieval behavior more consistent across differently phrased but equivalent queries.
7. Rewriting Can Introduce Errors
A rewritten query can accidentally drift away from the user's actual original intent.
A poorly rewritten query can retrieve worse results than the messy original would have.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A rewriting step that misinterprets a user's ambiguous phrasing can produce a confidently worded but incorrect query, retrieving results that seem plausible but actually miss the user's real intent entirely.

blocks.text: 8. Combining Rewriting With Expansion
Rewriting and expansion are not mutually exclusive, even though they change different parts of the query.
A rewritten, cleaner query can still be expanded with related terms afterward.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Pipeline order","Effect"],"rows":[["Rewrite, then expand","A clean query gets extra related terms added on top"],["Expand without rewriting","A messy query gets broadened, but ambiguity remains"]]}

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Query Rewriting Is Worth Applying

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Query Rewriting Is Worth Applying
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447443434-509137484.png
Conversational, messy, or ambiguous queries benefit most from rewriting.
Already clean, well formed queries, by contrast, gain little from further rewriting.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Confusing query rewriting with query expansion when they solve different problems.
Rewriting a query without conversation context, failing to resolve ambiguous pronouns correctly.
Trusting a rewritten query blindly without checking whether it drifted from the user's real intent.
Applying rewriting to already clean, well formed queries where it adds no value.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Query rewriting replaces a query's own wording with a clearer, more retrieval friendly version.
Unlike expansion, which adds terms, rewriting replaces the original wording entirely.
Real user queries often contain typos, incomplete sentences, or ambiguous pronouns.
A language model can rephrase a query into clearer, more complete retrieval ready language.
Rewriting with conversation context can resolve ambiguous pronouns into their actual subject.
Rewriting can standardize phrasing, making retrieval more consistent across equivalent queries.
A poorly rewritten query can drift from the user's real intent and retrieve worse results.
Rewriting and expansion are not mutually exclusive and can be combined together.
